stem: A solutions architect must add the ability to restore a production database to a specific point in time after an accidental delete, on top of the continuous replication already running. Which addition meets this?

choices.text: Increase the existing replication's frequency so the standby copy stays more closely in sync with the primary.
Enable AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode on the existing backup vault.
AWS Backup's scheduled, policy-based backups of the database, kept separately from the live replica.
Add a read replica of the database for reporting queries.

rationale: Scheduled, policy-based backups kept separately from the live replica are what provide restore points to choose from after an accidental delete, since replication alone only keeps a live copy of current data. Making replication faster keeps the standby copy more current with the primary, but a faster copy of an accidental delete is still a copy of the delete, so it does not add a restore point from before the delete happened. Vault Lock only locks the retention settings of backups that already exist in a vault; it governs how long an existing backup can be kept or deleted, but it does not itself schedule the policy-based backups that would create the missing restore point. A read replica is an asynchronous copy built to offload read traffic, not a set of restore points, so it does not provide a way to recover to a moment before the delete.
